title: Decoupling Spatio-Temporal Prediction: When Lightweight Large Models Meet Adaptive Hypergraphs

problem.claim: Spatio-temporal prediction supports applications including traffic management, climate monitoring, and energy scheduling.

gap.claim: Existing methods struggle to balance model expressiveness and computational efficiency when scaling to large real-world datasets.

contributions.claim: STH-SepNet decouples temporal and spatial modeling to improve efficiency and precision.
The framework models temporal dynamics with lightweight large language models and spatial interactions with an adaptive hypergraph neural network that dynamically constructs hyperedges.
A gating mechanism fuses temporal and spatial representations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present STH-SepNet as a novel framework for spatio-temporal prediction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on large-scale real-world datasets across multiple benchmarks demonstrate improved predictive performance while maintaining computational efficiency.
The authors describe STH-SepNet as a pragmatic and scalable solution for real-world spatio-temporal prediction.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatio-temporal prediction has broad practical applications.
Existing approaches face a scalability tradeoff between expressiveness and computational efficiency.
STH-SepNet separates temporal and spatial modeling, using lightweight large language models for temporal dynamics and adaptive hypergraphs for spatial interactions.
A gating mechanism fuses the temporal and spatial representations.
The authors report effectiveness across multiple benchmarks while maintaining computational efficiency.
